description: Key facts for this chapter, written by hand from the chapter text. Every entry links to the section that explains it.

people.name: Marcus Valerius Corvus
people.text: Consul who won at Mount Gaurus and Suessula in 343 BC.

people.name: Publius Decius Mus (father)
people.text: Junior officer who saved a trapped army by seizing a hilltop in 343 BC.

people.name: Quintus Publilius Philo
people.text: Commander at Naples whose command was extended: an early proconsul.

people.name: Gaius Pontius
people.text: Samnite commander who trapped the Romans at the Caudine Forks.

people.name: Herennius
people.text: Pontius’s father, who advised freeing all the Romans or killing them all.

people.name: Fabius Maximus Rullianus
people.text: Rome’s leading general, who crossed the Ciminian Forest and won at Sentinum.

people.name: Gellius Egnatius
people.text: Samnite commander who rallied the Etruscans and others against Rome.

people.name: Publius Decius Mus (son)
people.text: Consul who sacrificed his life (devotio) at Sentinum.

people.name: Lucius Papirius Cursor
people.text: Consul who took Aquilonia in 293 BC.

people.name: Livy
people.text: The Roman historian who is our main guide to these wars.

dates.text: Rome and the Samnites sign a treaty.
The Caudine Forks: a Roman army passes under the yoke.
Victory over the Etruscans at Lake Vadimo.
Peace ends the Great Samnite War.
Sentinum: Rome defeats Samnites, Etruscans, Umbrians and Gauls.
The last Samnite resistance is crushed.

terms.english: priests who demanded redress and declared war
“in place of a consul”: a proconsul
giving one’s life to the gods for victory
the Linen Legion, sworn never to flee
